decisions.decision: C core latency_comp now has two stages: Stage A (28-sample ADPCM-match delay on dry going into reverb send, gated on latency_comp + adpcm_enabled, unchanged) and Stage B (58-sample FIR-match delay on dry+ADPCM buses before master mixer, gated on latency_comp only, NEW).
decisions.rationale: Pre-fix, the plugin reported the FIR group delay through setLatencySamples but the dry path wasn't actually delayed by it. Host PDC over-compensated by 58-65 samples; passthrough configs couldn't null and dry+reverb mixes had 58 samples of transient pre-echo. Stage B aligns all three master-mix paths (dry/ADPCM/reverb) to the FIR group delay so the reported latency is accurate.

decisions.decision: Bit-faithful PS1 SPU behaviour preserved when latency_comp is OFF -- both stages no-op, dry races ahead of reverb (historically authentic smear). The Latency Comp toggle is the user-visible opt-in for modern-DAW correctness vs hardware fidelity.
decisions.rationale: Project North Star -- fixed-point quirks ARE the product; smoothing is opt-in. latency_comp default ON for modern DAW use, OFF for period-accurate testbed work.

decisions.decision: PLUG-15 closure used a headless null-test harness (tests/plugin/test_null_passthrough) at two host SRs (44.1k strict gate, 48k alignment+residual gates) rather than a continued Ardour GUI session.
decisions.rationale: Ardour's integer-only PDC can't null a 0.13-host-sample fractional misalignment with broadband content; that's a host limitation, not a plugin defect. The headless harness measures the plugin's actual properties (best-alignment cross-correlation, residual vs reported latency, fast-path strict null) which are what PLUG-15 cares about.

context_notes: Phase 22 was the v1.7 engineering risk hotspot per PITFALLS-v1.7.md: B1 RT-safety, B6 PDC alignment, C3 denormals. All three landed correctly. The Stage B latency_comp fix is a real product-quality improvement that affects all dry+reverb mixes in real DAWs (no more 58-sample pre-echo on dry transients), not just the null test. The headless null-test harness is a permanent regression gate; running it after any C core or SrcChain edit is the cheap way to catch latency-reporting drift.
